title: The sabbath without evening (13.35–13.36)
hookLine: a refrain you can hear coming, then silence: Genesis gives the seventh day no evening, and Augustine ends his book there
tomorrow: why does a book called Confessions open with praise, not sin?

cards: Some songs have a refrain you can feel coming before it lands; by the third time, you're singing it. The first chapter of Genesis has one. In the Douay-Rheims: "and there was evening and morning one day."
Then the second day, evening and morning. The third. A beat, like a clock ticking through creation.
Six times. Then the seventh day comes, God rests, and the beat just doesn't arrive. No evening.
No morning. Silence where the refrain should be. Augustine heard that silence, and he ended the Confessions inside it.

teach.b: Here's how he reads it. Everything God made is very good, Augustine says, and still it passes; those days had a morning and an evening. But the seventh day has no evening, because God made it holy to last.

teach.h: THE PEACE THAT HATH NO EVENING.
teach.b: So his last prayer in the book asks for peace: in the Pusey translation, "the peace of the Sabbath, which hath no evening." Then he turns it toward us.

teach.h: AFTER OUR WORKS, REST IN GOD.
teach.b: God rested after his works, he says, so that after ours, which are good only by God's gift, we too may rest in God, in the sabbath of eternal life. Listen to how far that reaches back.

teach.h: RESTLESS ON PAGE ONE, AT REST AT THE END.
teach.b: On the first page, the heart was restless until it rests in God. On the last, the rest arrives, and it's a day with no sunset, nothing ticking toward the end. The whole life story sits between those two lines.
That's something to tell a friend tonight: the Confessions doesn't end on Augustine at all.
It ends on Genesis, and on a rest that has no evening.

how: Catholics keep Sunday as the Lord's day of worship and rest, and pray for the dead with the words eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord; Augustine's 'sabbath without evening' names that hoped-for rest in God.

games.q: what does “the sabbath without evening” mean?
o: the Saturday market that closes before nightfall
a holiday when every lamp in the house stays lit
God's rest on day seven, a rest in God with no end

games.q: the last page — tap the pairs.
p: the peace that hath no evening
restless until it rests in God

s: the Confessions ends with the last events of Augustine's life
it ends with Genesis and the seventh day, a rest with no evening.
in Genesis 1, the seventh day has no evening-and-morning line
the refrain stops. Augustine read the silence as a rest that never ends.
Augustine's sabbath without evening means a weekly day off
he means rest in God, the sabbath of eternal life.

games.q: at a funeral, a friend who isn't Catholic hears the prayer eternal rest grant unto them and asks what kind of rest that means. which picture from today fits?
o: a rest in God, like a day with no evening to end it.
a long sleep, until the person is slowly forgotten.
a reward for having finally done enough good work.
games.why: Augustine hopes that after our works, good only by God's gift, we rest in God in the sabbath of eternal life: a peace that hath no evening.

practice: Let your hands fall open on your lap, palms up, and let your shoulders drop as if today's work were already finished. Stay like that, unhurried, the way a day rests when no evening is coming to end it.

wordCard.voice: The sabbath without evening. Augustine's last picture: God's rest on the seventh day, a rest in God that never ends.

carryVoice: Keep this one: a sabbath without evening, the rest the restless heart was looking for all along. Sleep well.
